mainTopic: The source for disqualifying a טבול יום, and רבה's question of why the תורה writes טמא, טבול יום and מחוסר כפורים separately
overview: The גמרא first wraps up an earlier discussion: every attempt to learn one disqualified group from another can be knocked down, so each rule stands on its own. Then it asks for the source that a טבול יום who does the עבודה makes it invalid. רבי סימאי uses the פסוק 'קדשים יהיו ולא יחללו', and since a טמא already has his own source in 'וינזרו', the פסוק is applied to a טבול יום. The גמרא asks why it should not apply instead to a כהן with a bald spot or a destroyed beard. It answers that the פסוק is linked to תרומה by a גזירה שוה, so it only covers people barred from תרומה, like a טבול יום. Next, רבה asks why the תורה wrote all three cases: טמא, טבול יום and מחוסר כפורים. He answers that each has its own stricter feature, so no single case can teach another. The גמרא pushes back that one case could be learned from the other two. It shows that מחוסר כפורים cannot be learned that way, but טבול יום seemingly can, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Each rule stays in its own place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the earlier back-and-forth. Every attempt to derive one disqualification from another can be refuted, so each one keeps its own separate source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you can refute it this way, and you can refute it that way. So each rule stays in its own place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing the previous discussion. It says none of the attempts to learn one disqualification from another really work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא tried to save פסוקים by learning one disqualified person from another. Each attempt had a weak point that could be attacked, because each case has something stricter about it. So the גמרא gives up on deriving them from each other, and every disqualification needs its own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: One can refute it (raise a difference that breaks the comparison)
Each and every one
Let it stand in its own place

steps.whatToRemember: No disqualification can be learned from another. Each one needs its own source in the תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the earlier comparison. Next, the גמרא moves on to the next item in the משנה's list, טבול יום.

phrases.english: Rather, one can refute it this way
and one can refute it that way,
each and every one shall stand in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ הָכִי וְאִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion that came before this text.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each disqualification needs its own independent source.

steps.title: What is the source for טבול יום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a טבול יום who does the עבודה makes it invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the rule about a טבול יום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks for the source of the משנה's rule about a טבול יום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום is a כהן who went to the מקוה today, but the sun has not set yet, so he is not fully pure. The משנה lists him among those whose עבודה is invalid, and the גמרא now asks for the פסוק behind that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who went to the מקוה today and waits for sunset to become fully pure
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: A טבול יום — from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know that the עבודה of a טבול יום is invalid, as the משנה says?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Because each rule needs its own source (Step 1), the גמרא now asks for the source for טבול יום.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that disqualifies the עבודה of a טבול יום.

steps.title: רבי סימאי brings the פסוק 'they shall not desecrate'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי סימאי: the hint that a טבול יום who does the עבודה makes it invalid comes from 'קדשים יהיו ולא יחללו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי סימאי says, where is the hint that a טבול יום who did the עבודה made it invalid? The פסוק says: 'They shall be holy and they shall not desecrate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא from רבי סימאי. It brings a פסוק about כהנים staying holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says כהנים must be holy and must not 'desecrate'. רבי סימאי reads 'desecrate' as also covering the עבודה: if an unfit כהן serves, the עבודה becomes invalid. He calls this only a 'hint' (רמז), because the פסוק does not say טבול יום openly.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint (not an open statement)
He desecrated (here: he made the עבודה invalid)
The פסוק says (introducing the source)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי סימאי says:
The hint for a טבול יום
that if he served, he desecrated the service — from where?
The פסוק says:
"They shall be holy and they shall not desecrate";

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'קדשים יהיו ולא יחללו' (ויקרא כא:ו).

steps.title: Why the פסוק goes to טבול יום and not to טמא
steps.stepSummary: A טמא כהן already has his own source in 'וינזרו', so this פסוק is free to teach about a טבול יום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is not needed for a טמא, who is learned from 'וינזרו', apply it to a טבול יום.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how we know this פסוק is about a טבול יום. The plain reading would fit a טמא, but he is already covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the method of 'אם אינו ענין': if a פסוק is not needed for its obvious subject, we use it for a nearby one. A fully טמא כהן is already disqualified from 'וינזרו', so the פסוק is free. The closest case is a טבול יום, who is still partly טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this subject
Apply it to a different subject
Impure
'And they shall separate themselves' (the source for a טמא כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the פסוק openly mentions טבול יום. We only reach טבול יום because the obvious subject (טמא) is already learned somewhere else.

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the subject of a טמא —
since that is derived from "And they shall separate themselves",
apply it to the subject of a טבול יום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the פסוק from Step 3 is applied to טבול יום.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since טמא is covered by 'וינזרו', the extra פסוק teaches about טבול יום.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק is about baldness or the beard instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why apply the free פסוק to טבול יום? Maybe it teaches that a כהן who made a bald spot or destroyed his beard ruins the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: apply it to someone who makes a bald spot, or who destroys the edge of his beard!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the derivation. It suggests a different topic that this extra פסוק could be teaching about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק right before talks about כהנים not making bald spots or destroying their beards. So those topics are even closer in the text than טבול יום. Maybe 'they shall not desecrate' means that such a כהן's עבודה is invalid, and then we have no source for טבול יום.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead (introducing another possibility)
One who makes a bald spot on his head
One who destroys the edge of his beard

phrases.english: Say instead: apply it to the subject
of one who makes a bald spot,
phrases.notes: This and the beard appear in the פסוק just before, ויקרא כא:ה.

phrases.english: and of one who destroys the edge of his beard!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'אם אינו ענין' move of Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the free פסוק specifically to טבול יום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The nearby topics of baldness and the beard are right next to the פסוק, so the free פסוק could just as easily teach that their עבודה is invalid.

steps.title: The פסוק is tied to תרומה, so it fits a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: The death penalty for a טבול יום who serves comes from a word-link ('חילול' and 'חילול') to תרומה. That link limits 'ולא יחללו' to people who are not allowed to eat תרומה. So it cannot apply to a כהן with a bald spot or a destroyed beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know a טבול יום who did the עבודה gets death? We learn 'profaning' here from 'profaning' by תרומה. So whoever is barred from תרומה ruins the עבודה, and whoever is not barred from תרומה does not ruin it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 5. The פסוק cannot be about a bald-spot כהן, because it is linked to תרומה, and only a טבול יום is barred from תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a word-link between 'יחללו' in our פסוק and 'יחללוהו' by תרומה. This link does two things. It gives a טבול יום who serves a death penalty, and it limits the rule to people who are disqualified from תרומה. A כהן with a bald spot or a destroyed beard may still eat תרומה, so he is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: with death (by the hand of Heaven)
learns 'profaning' from 'profaning' (a word-link between two פסוקים)
the holy portion given to כהנים
profanes (ruins) the Temple service

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new question. The 'מנא לן' here is the first part of the answer to step 5. It shows that the פסוק is already connected to תרומה, so it cannot be moved over to the bald-spot כהן.
steps.whyThisMatters: The test 'barred from תרומה' becomes the dividing line. It decides which disqualified כהנים ruin the עבודה through this פסוק.

phrases.english: One who immersed that day, that if he served, he is liable to death,
phrases.notes: This is the answer to the last challenge. The פסוק is already being used for the טבול יום.

phrases.english: from where do we know it?
Because he learns 'profaning'–'profaning' from תרומה;
one who disqualifies תרומה profanes the service,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא פָּסֵיל בִּתְרוּמָה – לָא מַחֵיל עֲבוֹדָה.
phrases.english: one who does not disqualify תרומה does not profane the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: טבול יום דאם עבד במיתה מנא לן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by showing why the פסוק can only refer to a טבול יום.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source limitation through a word-link (גזירה שוה) to תרומה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The free פסוק could teach that a bald-spot or beard-destroying כהן ruins the עבודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is linked to תרומה, so it only covers people barred from תרומה, like a טבול יום.

steps.title: רבה asks why all three cases are written
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks why the תורה needed to write separately that a טמא, a טבול יום, and a מחוסר כפורים each ruin the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Why do I need the תורה to write a טמא, a טבול יום, and a מחוסר כפורים?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רבה asks why the תורה lists three separate disqualified people instead of just one, and this sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the גמרא expects that one case could teach the others. So writing all three looks like extra words. רבה is asking what each case adds that we could not work out without it.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it?
the Merciful One (the תורה)
one who still needs to bring his atonement קרבן

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Why do I need that the Merciful One wrote
an impure one, and one who immersed that day, and one lacking atonement?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבה למה לי דכתב רחמנא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about why all three disqualifications are needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תורה writes all three disqualified cases instead of just one.

steps.title: Each case has its own stricter feature
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that all three are needed. A טמא makes other things impure. A טבול יום is barred from תרומה. A מחוסר כפורים still has an action left to do. So no single case can teach another.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all needed. If the תורה wrote only טמא, I would say that is because he makes others impure. If it wrote only טבול יום, מחוסר כפורים could not be learned from it, because a טבול יום is barred from תרומה. If it wrote only מחוסר כפורים, טבול יום could not be learned from it, because a מחוסר כפורים still lacks an action.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers his own question. He shows that each case has something stricter about it, so we could not learn the others from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To learn one case from another, the source case cannot be 'stronger'. A טמא is stronger because he spreads impurity. A טבול יום is stronger because he cannot eat תרומה. A מחוסר כפורים is stronger because he still has to bring his קרבן, while a טבול יום only waits for nightfall.

keyTerms.meaning: they are needed (each one teaches something)
since (this one has a stricter feature)
makes others impure
cannot be learned from it
still lacking an action

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the direction. Each stricter feature is the reason the OTHER cases cannot be learned from this one, because this one is stronger.

phrases.english: They are necessary;

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא טָמֵא – שֶׁכֵּן מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.english: for had the Merciful One written impure, I would say it is because he imparts impurity.
Had it written it with one who immersed that day;
one lacking atonement could not be derived from it,
since he is disqualified from תרומה.
Had it written it with one lacking atonement;
one who immersed that day could not be derived from it,
since he is lacking an action.
phrases.notes: He still has to bring his קרבן. A טבול יום only needs to wait for nightfall.

steps.triggerLanguage: צריכי דאי כתב רחמנא טמא שכן מטמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's question by showing that each case has a unique stricter feature.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No single case can teach another, because each has its own stricter feature: making others impure, being barred from תרומה, or still lacking an action.

steps.title: Learn one case from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: true, one case cannot teach another, but one case could be learned from the other two together.
steps.simpleTranslation: From one case it cannot be learned; let one be learned from the other two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's answer. It agrees that one case alone is not enough, but it argues that two cases together should be able to teach the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the stricter features differ, two cases can be combined to cover each other's weak points. So the תורה should only need two of the cases, and the third should come by itself. This sets up the next answer, which must show why even that does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: from one
let it come (be learned)
from two

phrases.english: From one it cannot be derived;
let one be derived from two!

steps.triggerLanguage: מחדא לא אתי תיתי חדא מתרתי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer by suggesting that two cases together could teach the third.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that all three cases must be written.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if one case alone has a stricter feature, two cases together could cancel out each other's stricter features and teach the third, so one of the three would be extra.

steps.title: Which case could the תורה have left out?
steps.stepSummary: Following the previous push-back, the גמרא asks which of the three cases the תורה could have skipped and learned from the other two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one should the Merciful One not have written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks which of the three cases could be the one that is learned from the other two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 claimed that one case could be learned from the other two combined. To test that, the גמרא must pick a specific case and check whether it really can be learned that way. The next steps try each option.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one?
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Let it not write. Meaning: the פסוק would not be needed.

phrases.english: Which one should the Merciful One not write?
phrases.notes: He means: which of the three (טמא, טבול יום, מחוסר כפורים) could the תורה have left out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the claim from step 9 by asking which specific case would be the extra one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three cases is the one that could be learned from the other two together.

steps.title: The case of one still owing a sacrifice cannot be left out
steps.stepSummary: The first attempt is to skip מחוסר כפורים and learn him from טמא and טבול יום. It is rejected, because those two are both barred from תרומה and he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose the תורה did not write the law about a מחוסר כפורים, and we learned it from these other two. That fails: what about these two? They are special because they are barred from eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries leaving out the מחוסר כפורים and learning his law from the other two. Then it knocks that idea down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא and a טבול יום share a strict feature: neither may eat תרומה. A מחוסר כפורים may eat תרומה, so he is milder than both of them. Maybe a milder person does not ruin the עבודה, so his case could not be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who became pure but still has to bring his atonement sacrifice
Let it be learned from these (other cases)
What about these? This is the standard way to point out what makes the source cases special.
Not allowed to eat תרומה

phrases.english: Let it not write about one lacking atonement
and let it come from these:
phrases.notes: "These" means the טמא and the טבול יום together.

phrases.english: what about these?
They are barred from תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לִכְתּוֹב בִּמְחוּסַּר כִּפּוּרִים וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first possible answer to step 10 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the idea of learning מחוסר כפורים from the other two.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both source cases share a strict feature (barred from תרומה) that the מחוסר כפורים does not have.

steps.title: Instead, the case of one who immersed today can be left out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that טבול יום is the case the תורה did not need, since it can be learned from טמא and מחוסר כפורים together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the Merciful One did not need to write the law about a טבול יום. It could be learned from these other two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a better answer to step 10: skip the טבול יום and learn him from the טמא and the מחוסר כפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה did write the טבול יום case. So if this works, writing it seems unnecessary, which supports the challenge of step 9. The next step checks whether this suggestion can be knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This brings in a new suggestion.
Someone who immersed today but must wait until nightfall to be fully pure

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּטְבוּל יוֹם,
phrases.english: Rather, let the Merciful One not write about one who immersed that day,
and let it come from these;
phrases.notes: Here "these" means the טמא and the מחוסר כפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּטְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion of step 11 with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The טבול יום case is the one that could be learned from the other two together.

steps.title: The objection about a missing action does not hold
steps.stepSummary: The possible objection is that both טמא and מחוסר כפורים still lack an action. The גמרא rejects it, because the impurity of a מחוסר כפורים is weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: What objection could you raise? That these two are special because each still has an action left to do? In the end, their impurity is weak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a possible objection to learning טבול יום from the other two, and then shows that the objection does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection: a טמא still needs to immerse, and a מחוסר כפורים still needs to bring his sacrifice, while a טבול יום only waits for nightfall. The answer: the impurity of a מחוסר כפורים is very weak, since he may even eat תרומה. If someone that mild still ruins the עבודה, then a טבול יום, whose impurity is stronger, surely does. So "missing an action" is not what makes these cases strict.

keyTerms.meaning: What can you refute with? It means no good objection is left.
Still missing an action they must do
In the end, after all
Weak, thin

steps.whatToRemember: טבול יום is the case that could have been learned from טמא and מחוסר כפורים together. This leaves the question of why the תורה wrote it at all.
steps.confusionAlert: "Their impurity is weak" is about the מחוסר כפורים. His impurity is milder than a טבול יום's, so his "missing action" does not make him stricter.
steps.whyThisMatters: If טבול יום can be learned from the other two, writing it looks extra, so רבה's question of why all three are written comes back. The discussion continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: For what would you refute with?
What about these, that they still lack an action?
phrases.notes: The טמא still has to immerse, and the מחוסר כפורים still has to bring his sacrifice.

phrases.english: In the end, their impurity is weak.
phrases.notes: He means the מחוסר כפורים: his impurity is so mild that he may even eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the answer of step 12 by rejecting the one possible objection to it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the possible objection that the two source cases both still lack an action.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מחוסר כפורים has weak impurity, so missing an action does not make him stricter than a טבול יום.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טבול יום can be learned from טמא and מחוסר כפורים together.
